name: COB — HSA secondary with the primary's deductible: set the COB indicators, correct the deductible and Pay
description: Eleven steps mapping onto the HS1.1 source document: identify the PX_HS1 hard edit and check the hierarchy, find the Limited Liability record is on file and updated, confirm the secondary plan is an HSA plan, validate, set the COB indicators on the Claim Header, read what validation did to the deductible, move that amount to Non-covered under the right EOB code, validate again to clear the deductible, and pay.

steps.name: Identify the HS1 hard edit and check the event hierarchy
steps.description: Open the Event Resolution tab. All Edits lists every edit on the claim, with PX_HS1 the hard edit highlighted with an error indication — that is the event you are resolving. PX_HS1 fires on a member with two insurance policies where the primary insurer has already processed the claim and applied the full allowed amount to its own deductible; when the secondary plan is an HSA plan, applying a second deductible would charge the member twice for the same claim, and HS1 is the workaround that prevents it. Read the rest of the list against the established hierarchy to check whether any event must be resolved before PX_HS1. If one is present, resolve it first; if none is, proceed. The six events beside it are informational, so nothing of higher priority is present and you proceed.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Event Resolution tab is opened while this step is active. Visits only fire on a user click, so the trainee opens it deliberately.
steps.hint: On 'Event Resolution', All Edits lists PX_HS1 as the hard edit with six informational events beside it. Nothing of higher priority is listed, so no event blocks the review.
steps.checklistItem: Identify the HS1 hard edit and check the event hierarchy

steps.name: Check whether the LL record is updated
steps.description: Open the Search tab and its Limited Liability sub-tab, then review the Limited Liability (LL) records to determine whether an update has been completed. If the record has been updated, carry on with claim processing; if it has not, follow the routing guidelines and request a COB update. One record is on file — Type COB, effective 01/01/2026, no End date, Order of benefits 'S - Our Insurance is secondary' — so the coordination order is established and Our Insurance is the secondary plan. Here the record is updated, so go to the next step.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Search → Limited Liability sub-tab is opened while this step is active.
steps.hint: On 'Search → Limited Liability', one record is listed: Type COB, effective 01/01/2026, End date blank, 'S - Our Insurance is secondary'. Open it and read the Updated date — the record has been updated, so no COB update is needed and you carry on.
steps.checklistItem: Check whether the LL record is updated

steps.name: Verify the secondary plan is an HSA plan
steps.description: Review the member information to determine the plan type of the secondary policy. Open the Search tab and its Member sub-tab, scroll to the Group Information panel below the member results, and open the Group Additional Information section to read the Product field. If the plan is an HSA plan, carry on with the remaining HS1 steps; if it is not, stop following them and process the claim under the standard guidelines. The Product field reads HSA POS, so the secondary plan is an HSA plan and you proceed.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Group Additional Information section is opened. The section stays shut — and its Product field unreadable — until this step is active.
steps.hint: On 'Search → Member', scroll to the Group Information panel and click the 'Group Additional Information' section header. Read the Product field.
steps.checklistItem: Verify the secondary plan is an HSA plan

steps.name: Validate benefits and confirm the deductible applied
steps.description: Click Validate on the claim summary bar so the claim processes under the plan's benefits, then check on the Claim Lines tab whether the allowed amount is accumulating toward the deductible. If the deductible is being applied, carry on; if it is not, this workflow does not apply and the claim follows standard processing. Here the entire allowed amount is applied to the deductible — nothing errors and nothing warns, which is exactly why HS1 exists: the primary has already taken this deductible, and left alone the secondary would take it again.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes on the FIRST press of the claim-summary Validate control while this step is active. The same control completes step_010 on its second press, after the deductible has been moved to Non-covered. Validate carries no guard of its own — the step order is what holds it back.
steps.hint: Click Validate on the claim summary bar, then open 'Claim Lines' and look at the Allowed and Deductible columns on line 1.
steps.checklistItem: Validate benefits and confirm the deductible applied

steps.name: Open the Claim Header to update the COB indicators
steps.description: Navigate to the Claim Header tab to update the COB Rule. The Benefit Indicators section carries the COB and COB Rule fields, which read 0 and - as the claim arrived. Both are set here, before the deductible is corrected, so the claim records how the coordination was applied.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Claim Header tab is opened while this step is active. Visits only fire on a user click, so the trainee opens it deliberately.
steps.hint: Click the 'Claim Header' tab and find the Benefit Indicators section, where COB reads 0 and COB Rule reads -.
steps.checklistItem: Open the Claim Header to update the COB indicators

steps.name: Enter COB Rule J and COB Yes
steps.description: In the Benefit Indicators section on the Claim Header tab, update the COB Rule field to J and the COB field to Yes, replacing the - and the 0 the claim arrived with. Together they record on the claim that the coordination was applied and under which rule. Check both read back correctly before moving on.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the COB Rule box holds J. A step grades one field against one expected value, so the COB entry beside it is instructed and highlighted rather than separately graded.
steps.hint: Under 'Benefit Indicators', type J into the COB Rule box and Yes into the COB box.
steps.checklistItem: Enter COB Rule J and COB Yes

steps.name: Review the updated deductible amount
steps.description: Open the Claim Lines tab and read the updated deductible on line 1: the full allowed amount of $250.00 has accumulated to the deductible. Because the primary insurer has already applied this same $250.00 to its own deductible, leaving it here would apply a second deductible to one claim and charge the member twice. The $250.00 must therefore be moved to Non-covered under the EOB code that records why.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Claim Lines tab is opened while this step is active.
steps.hint: On 'Claim Lines', line 1 now shows Allowed $250.00 and Deductible $250.00 against Billed $250.00.

steps.name: Enter the Non-covered amount of $250
steps.description: In the Line 1 — Non-covered entry section on the Claim Lines tab, enter the deductible amount of 250 in the Non-covered box. This moves the amount off the secondary's deductible, so the member is not charged a deductible the primary has already taken.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes only when the Non-covered box holds 250. The EOB code is graded separately by the next step, so entering one value earns one step.
steps.hint: Type 250 into the Non-covered box under 'Line 1 — Non-covered entry'.

steps.name: Enter EOB code 00003
steps.description: In the same section, enter 00003 in the EOB code box. The code is what records on the claim why the amount is non-covered — the primary insurer has already applied it to its deductible. Confirm both values are entered correctly before moving on.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes only when the EOB code box holds 00003. Entering it in the Non-covered box instead completes neither step.
steps.hint: Type 00003 into the EOB code box beside Non-covered.

steps.name: Click Validate on the claim summary a second time
steps.description: Click on the Validate button on the claim summary. This is the same control as step 4, pressed again now that the $250.00 has been moved to Non-covered under EOB code 00003. The claim re-processes against the corrected line: the deductible comes off, so the member is not charged a deductible the primary insurer has already taken, and the claim is ready to be processed.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes on the SECOND press of the claim-summary Validate control. The first press completes step_004; this press counts only once the Non-covered amount and the EOB code are entered, which is what step order guarantees.
steps.hint: Click 'Validate' on the claim summary bar again — the same button as step 4. The deductible on the claim line then clears.
steps.checklistItem: Click Validate on the claim summary a second time
steps.completionToast: Benefits re-applied — the deductible is cleared.

steps.name: Submit the Pay decision
steps.description: The COB indicators are set, the double deductible has been moved to Non-covered and the claim has been re-validated, so it can now be processed. Select Pay from the Decision dropdown on the claim summary and click Submit.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes only when the claim is submitted with Pay. Deny or Pend does not complete it.
steps.hint: Choose 'Pay' from the Decision dropdown on the claim summary bar and click Submit.
